Looping you all — Nexus has a hard date in November and is seeing preemption from Kestrel's burst. They want an explicit guarantee or a minimal MPA amendment.

- Nexus is on a reserved lane (monthly commit) with allowed burst.
- Kestrel is in the same physical GPU pool; current routing rules favor earliest reservation but burst behavior is muddy when autoscaler triggers nodes.

Can ops/strategy propose a short-term triage (2 weeks) and a contract change path? I'm happy to join a call if helpful.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity sizing — Nexus/Kestrel overlap

Thanks Rafael — quick triage and suggested remediation below. I attached a heatmap I generated from the forecast Elena sent.

Proposed short-term (2 week) triage:
- Reserve policy shift: temporarily pin Nexus to physical pool A-02 during 02:00–10:00 UTC (their heavy nightly runs). This requires moving 3 low-utilization burst reservations from A-02 -> A-05.
- Canary routing: route 20% of Kestrel burst through fallback pool B for 48 hours to measure impact.
- Spike protection: enable soft-throttle for bursts exceeding 60% of pool capacity for both tenants; notify CMs via webhook.

Trade-offs / risk:
- Moving burst reservations will degrade Kestrel tail latency slightly during non-peak but preserves Nexus launch window.
- Requires a quick configuration push and a one-line contract addendum for Nexus if we are to pin pools for the full launch month.

Next steps:
1) Ops to confirm no infra blockers on pool remapping (Karthik).
2) Legal/sales to prepare a 1-paragraph MPA addendum (Rafael / Markus).
3) Schedule a 30-min triage call with Nexus + Kestrel (I can host) — propose Wed 10:00 PT.

Attachments: capacity_heatmap_q3.xlsx (XLSX, 115KB)

--
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Jul 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity sizing — Nexus/Kestrel overlap

Thanks Monica — a few operational constraints to call out: 

- Pool remaps are possible but we cannot change reserved slice allocations without a committed deal amendment; remapping burst reservations (non-committed) is straightforward.
- Canary routing for 20% is low risk; we'll need a short maintenance window to adjust autoscaler weights (≈ 12 minutes).
- Enabling soft-throttle is a code flag we can flip, but we must monitor KV cache eviction behavior — I recommend enabling it behind a flag and running the canary for 72h, not 48h.

Options we can present to Nexus:
A) Quick patch (no contract change): remap bursts + 72h canary + soft-throttle flag. This will reduce preemption risk for launch but is not a contractual guarantee.
B) Contract path (recommended for strong guarantee): 1-paragraph MPA addendum to pin Nexus's reserved slice to pool A-02 for Nov launch window; bill small premium for pool pinning. Legal lead time 3–5 business days.

I'll start scheduling the maintenance window and spin up monitoring dashboards. Will follow up with ETA on the config push.

- Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Rafael / Monica / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick responses. For product launch risk tolerance we need stronger assurances than a temporary patch. Option B (MPA addendum + pin) is acceptable — Nexus can approve a one-paragraph amendment that pins the reserved slice for the full Nov 1–30 window. Procurement will need draft language and an estimate for cost delta.

We are happy to sign a short addendum and process expedited PO once we have the wording. Also looping in Kestrel procurement so they can coordinate scheduling (we prefer not to displace their burst entirely).

Please send the draft and estimated delta by EOD Thu so we can route it internally.

Best,
Elena
